substantive_evaluations.collective_statement_most_likely_to_succ: Candidate 01__19560031-RESPONSE-10182026.tex represents the most comprehensive, legally sound, and procedurally robust transmittal and response document in the cluster. It impeccably addresses every formal and financial deficiency identified in the Notice to File Missing Parts mailed August 18, 2026. Specifically: (1) it correctly calculates the rollover statutory deadline under 35 U.S.C. § 21(b) and 37 CFR § 1.7 from Sunday, October 18, 2026 to Monday, October 19, 2026; (2) it details the complete curative envelope (Documents 01–09) including standalone replacement claims (37 CFR § 1.75(h)), replacement abstract (37 CFR § 1.72(b)), formal drawings (37 CFR § 1.84), perfected AIA declaration (37 CFR § 1.63), and substitute specification under 37 CFR § 1.125(c); (3) it contains an explicit 37 CFR § 1.125(b) certification of no new matter explaining the excision of embedded drawings, segregation of claims/abstract, and preemptive deletion of the Government License Grant to protect Small Entity status under 37 CFR § 1.27; and (4) it implements the exact Path B knapsack optimization under 37 CFR § 1.22(b) and MPEP § 509 ($70 to Code 4011 and $308 to Code 2111, with $592 in unpaid base fees plus the $60 suspension fee tendered concurrently at checkout). Moreover, unlike the other drafts, it astutely flags the accounting discrepancy between the Notice ($398 credited) and the Filing Receipt ($484 received) for Application Assistance Unit reconciliation, maintaining professional decorum without adversarial friction.
